**Refined prompt:** Diagnose why the RealWorld React client throws `Cannot read property 'slug' of undefined` immediately after article creation while the NestJS server logs nothing — answering as a reader of this codebase, citing the actual lines, distinguishing verified cause from speculation, and ending with the concrete fix.

## What's wrong

`POST /api/articles` is the one handler that does not return the RealWorld envelope. It responds with a bare `ArticleEntity`, so the client's `response.article` is `undefined` and `.slug` throws.

Two lines, in the two layers that should each have caught it:

- `src/article/article.service.ts:170` — `async create(...): Promise<ArticleEntity>` and `src/article/article.service.ts:186` — `return newArticle;` (bare entity, no wrapper).
- `src/article/article.controller.ts:52-54` — `async create(...)` has **no return type annotation** at all, so TypeScript never compared it against `ArticleRO`. Every sibling handler is annotated (`findOne` → `Promise<ArticleRO>` at `article.controller.ts:39`, `findAll` → `Promise<ArticlesRO>` at `:25`).

Compare against every other article path, which all return `{article}`: `findOne` (`article.service.ts:98`), `update` (`:194`), `favorite` (`:144`), `unFavorite` (`:162`), `addComment` (`:111`).

So the wire response is `{"id":1,"slug":"how-to-train-your-dragon-xk29fq",...}` where the client expects `{"article":{...}}`.

## Why the server logs nothing

There is nothing to log. The insert succeeded, Nest serialized the returned object and sent `201`. The crash is entirely client-side — the `TypeError` happens in the browser when the React app reads `res.article.slug` to redirect to the new article page. No exception filter, no interceptor, no 500. I confirmed there is no global response interceptor that could have been adding the envelope elsewhere: `src/main.ts:5-21` registers only the global prefix and Swagger.

This is `LESSONS.md:49-57` (#57) verbatim — the lesson is recorded but the code was never fixed, or it regressed.

## The fix

```ts
// src/article/article.service.ts:170
async create(userId: number, articleData: CreateArticleDto): Promise<ArticleRO> {
  ...
  return {article: newArticle};   // :186
}

// src/article/article.controller.ts:52
async create(@User('id') userId: number, @Body('article') articleData: CreateArticleDto): Promise<ArticleRO> {
```

`ArticleRO` is already imported in both files (`article.service.ts:10`, `article.controller.ts:5`). The controller annotation is the part that keeps this from happening again — with it, the bare-entity return is a compile error.

## Two things you will hit immediately after

Both are in the same `create()` and will bite the moment the redirect succeeds:

1. **`body` is never written.** `create()` copies `title`, `description`, `slug`, `tagList`, `comments` (`article.service.ts:173-177`) but not `articleData.body`, even though the DTO declares it (`dto/create-article.dto.ts:4`) and the column exists with `default: ''` (`article.entity.ts:20-21`). Every created article saves with an empty body and no error.
2. **The created payload has no `author`.** The relation is only set from the inverse side (`author.articles.push(article)`, `article.service.ts:182`), and `newArticle` is the pre-relation save result — so the response object has no `author` key. Any client reading `article.author.username` off the create response gets the same class of crash. It's also missing `favorited` / `favoritesCount` / `createdAt` / `updatedAt`, which is the spec-conformance item already open in `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:7-9`.

**What I did not read:** the React client itself (not in this workspace — the `response.article.slug` access is inferred from the spec contract described in `.claude/knowledge/workspace.md:73` and the symptom you reported), and the `prisma/` folder, which `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:23-25` marks as not the production path.

Want me to apply the envelope fix, and fold in the missing `body` assignment while I'm in there?
